new_statements.quote: [p.49] 3-1 Note liminaire. Dans le parler pòŋààl, l'intensité d'articulation est dénuée de valeur significative. [...] Un autre type d'opposition existe dans la langue de Boum Kabir : il s'agit de la hauteur mélodique, apte à différencier deux unités phonématiquement identiques. [...] [p.50] l'hypothèse du pòŋààl comme langue à accent syllabique de hauteur [...] En fait, pareille hypothèse multipliait les problèmes qu'elle tentait de résoudre. [...] Au bout du compte, les données toléraient mieux l'analyse du pòŋààl comme langue à tons, c'est-à-dire une langue dans laquelle chaque syllabe est dotée de hauteur (relative) déterminée. [...] deux hauteurs seulement interviennent de manière significative : ce sont les deux « tons » dits haut et bas.
new_statements.translation: 3-1 Preliminary note. In the pòŋààl dialect, articulatory intensity has no distinctive value. [...] Another type of opposition exists in the language of Boum Kabir: melodic pitch, able to differentiate two phonemically identical units. [...] [p.50] the hypothesis of pòŋààl as a language with a syllabic pitch accent [...] In fact, such a hypothesis multiplied the problems it tried to solve. [...] In the end, the data were better accommodated by the analysis of pòŋààl as a tone language, i.e. a language in which every syllable carries a determined (relative) pitch. [...] only two pitch levels are significant: the two 'tones' called high and low.
new_statements.citation: Pairault, Claude. 1969. Documents du parler d'Iro, kùláál du Tchad. Paris: Librairie C. Klincksieck (Langues et littératures de l'Afrique noire, 5).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: exists and contains every fragment of the reported quote at the stated locators (§3-1 p.49, §3-3 pp.50-51 with n.3, §3-4 p.51). The file is not a page scan but a reconstruction chained from Google Books full-text snippets of volume nFkHAQAAIAAJ; the raw receipts in gbooks/337 lines) carry each quoted sentence as returned by Google: line 95/106 'Dans le parler pòŋààl, l'intensité d'articulation est dénuée de valeur significative. Nous avons d'autre part rendu compte, en phonématique...'; lines 161-172 '...hypothèse du pònààl comme langue à accent syllabique de hauteur, accent marqué de façon mélodique par une opposition haut : bas. Dans cette perspective, un seul noyau syllabique…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kulaal (reference dialect pòŋààl of Boum Kabir) is analysed as a two-tone language (H, L; every syllable tone-bearing, contour tones on long vowels); intensity (dynamic stress) is explicitly stated to be non-distinctive, and an earlier one-pitch-accent-per-word analysis (Pairault 1966: 423) is explicitly rejected. No positional word-stress rule is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None as to stress. Extra (3rd/4th) pitch registers attributed to expressive intonation or register shift ('décalage de registration') at clause/sentence boundaries. Footnote 3 (p.50) explicitly leaves 'intact and unexplored' a possible word-accent treatment (à la Rowlands on Mandinka); Pairault later (Cahiers du LUTO 1981; 1994: 29 n.14; 2001) doubted that every syllable bears significant pitch and suggested Kulaal might rather be a 'langue à accents de hauteur' with two heights and two lengths — never worked out, and no linguist has since re-examined Kulaal prosody (Boyeldieu et al. 2018: 12).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the word/moneme in the pòŋààl dialect (Boum Kabir), Pairault's reference variety; based on texts and lexicon, impressionistic (no instrumental data). Access caveat: the 1969 text was read only through chained Google Books full-text snippets (book has no preview); page numbers from Google's search-within-volume hits and from Boyeldieu et al. 2018's citation 'Pairault 1969: 49-54'. Verification against the printed pages is desirable.
new_statements.identity_note: All statements concern the pòŋààl dialect of Kulaal spoken at Boum Kabir (Boum-le-Grand), Pairault's reference variety; Pairault 1969:11 distinguishes four varieties (páṭóól, pòŋààl, tɩ́ààlà, tííṭààl), all under gula1265 [glj]. Do not confuse with 'Kulaale' [kʊ̀láːlɛ̀], a Fania/Fanya variety (fani1244) documented by Lionnet (LDD 17, 2020), nor with Bon Gula/Zan Gula ('Goula du Guéra').

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Raimund Kastenholz, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer & Florian Lionnet. 2018. The Bua Group languages (Chad, Adamawa 13): A comparative perspective. In R. Kramer & R. Kießling (eds.), Current approaches to Adamawa and Gur languages, 53-126. Köln: Köppe. [HAL preprint halshs-03096908, 58 pp.]
sources.note: §4.4 Tones (preprint p.12): 'Kulaal, however, differs from all these languages in that it has only two tones (Pairault 1966: 423; 1969: 49-54)', then quotes in translation Pairault 1994:29 n.14 doubting that Kulaal is a tone language in which each syllable bears a relevant pitch. Feature table marks Kulaal as lacking verb tone contrast. No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the paper.

sources.note: Repeats the doubt: analysed the parler d'Iro as a 'langue à tons' (all syllable pitches significant) — 'Est-ce juste ? Je n'en suis pas sûr du tout. Mais, depuis quarante ans, aucun linguiste apparemment ne s'est aventuré sur les bords d'Iro pour s'attaquer au problème.' Confirms no later fieldwork on Kulaal prosody as of 2001.
